    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    40	
    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    44	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    45	
    46	open scoped TensorProduct
    47	
    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    49	
    50	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    51	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    52	
    53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    54	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    55	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    58	
    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    72	  datum_class :
    73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
    80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
    87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    90	  h0_rank_one :
    91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    93	
    94	namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    95	
    96	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    97	
    98	noncomputable local instance presentationModuleSections
    99	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) (U : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens) :
   100	    Module P.cover.Carrier Γ(P.module, U) :=
   101	  Scheme.moduleKSections
   102	    (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module U
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.
   105	
   106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
   107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   109	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   110	    B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] (Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B]
   111	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   112	  P.datum.datumH0BaseChange B
   113	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing)
   114	
   115	/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
   116	noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   117	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   119	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   120	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ⟶
   121	      P.module :=
   122	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   123	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module
   124	
   125	/-! ## Native pushforward base change and evaluation coherence -/
   126	
   127	/-- The canonical native pushforward base-change isomorphism supplied by the presentation.
   128	
   129	The isomorphism is not chosen independently: its hom is definitionally
   130	`(canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module`. -/
   131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   135	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   136	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   137	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj
   138	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   139	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   140	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) := by
   141	  exact @asIso _ _ _ _ ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module)
   142	    (P.native_pushforward_base_change g f' g' sq)
   143	
   144	/-- The native pushforward base-change isomorphism for an affine coefficient extension. -/
   145	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIsoAffine (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   146	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   147	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   148	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   149	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier B)))).obj
   150	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   151	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   152	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   153	        (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))).obj
   154	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)).obj P.module) :=
   155	  P.nativeBaseChangeIso
   156	    (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B).left
   157	    (snd C (overSpec k B)).left
   158	    (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)
   159	    (Over.isPullback_whiskerLeft C (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B))
   160	
   161	/-- The source of evaluation identifies canonically with the source of evaluation after any
   162	cartesian base change. -/
   163	noncomputable def evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   164	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   165	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   166	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   167	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   168	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   169	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   170	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⋙
   171	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj
   172	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   173	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   174	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback f').obj
   175	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) :=
   176	  ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
   177	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
   178	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g'
   179	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).symm).app
   180	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward

181	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   182	
   183	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   184	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   185	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   186	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   187	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   188	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   189	
   190	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   191	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   192	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   193	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   194	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi
   195	
   196	/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
   197	The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
   198	theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
   199	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   200	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   201	    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
   202	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   203	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property
   204	
   205	end
   206	
   207	end AlgebraicGeometry

181	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).symm) ≪≫
   182	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').mapIso (P.nativeBaseChangeIso g f' g' sq)
   183	
   184	/-- Under the source identification, evaluation after base change is the pullback of the
   185	presentation's original evaluation counit. -/
   186	theorem evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso_hom_evaluation
   187	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   188	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   189	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   190	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   191	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   192	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   193	    (P.evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso g f' g' sq).hom ≫
   194	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
   195	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) =
   196	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map P.evaluation := by
   197	  change ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
   198	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
   199	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g'
   200	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).symm).inv).app
   201	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   202	            (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)) ≫
   203	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module) ≫
   204	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
   205	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module)) =
   206	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
   207	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   208	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module)
   209	  exact canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel sq P.module
   210	
   211	/-! The affine coefficient-extension spelling of the evaluation/base-change contract.
   212	
   213	This is the consumer-facing specialization for the future zero-locus construction: it keeps
   214	the coefficient ring `B` and `relCurveMap` explicit while retaining the canonical cartesian
   215	square, rather than introducing a second base-change witness. -/
   216	theorem evaluationSourceBaseChangeIsoAffine_hom_evaluation
   217	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   218	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   219	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   220	    (P.evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso
   221	      (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B).left
   222	      (snd C (overSpec k B)).left
   223	      (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)
   224	      (Over.isPullback_whiskerLeft C
   225	        (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B))).hom ≫
   226	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   227	          (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).counit.app
   228	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)).obj P.module) =
   229	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)).map P.evaluation := by
   230	  exact P.evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso_hom_evaluation
   231	    (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B).left
   232	    (snd C (overSpec k B)).left
   233	    (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)
   234	    (Over.isPullback_whiskerLeft C (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B))
   235	
   236	/-! ## The datum/native-section/evaluation bridge -/
   237	
   238	/-- The global datum section represented by a degree-zero cohomology class. -/
   239	noncomputable def datumSection (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   240	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   241	    P.datum.sheaf.obj.obj (op (⊤ : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens)) :=
   242	  Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   243	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   244	    isTerminalTop P.datum.sheaf y
   245	
   246	/-! The datum-side section after coefficient extension.  This deliberately stops at the
   247	glued cocycle sheaf; identifying it with native `Scheme.Modules` global sections is a
   248	separate contract and is not smuggled in here. -/
   249	noncomputable def datumSectionBaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   250	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   251	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B]
   252	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   253	    (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf.obj.obj
   254	      (op (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)) :=
   255	  Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   256	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   257	    isTerminalTop (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf
   258	    (P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y))
   259	
   260	/-- H⁰ base change transports the tied datum section to the canonical glued-section map. -/
   261	theorem datumSectionBaseChange_one_tmul (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   262	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   263	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B]
   264	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   265	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y =
   266	      P.datum.sectionsMapTop B (P.datumSection y) := by
   267	  exact P.datum.linearEquiv₀_datumH0BaseChange_one_tmul B
   268	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing) y
   269	
   270	/-- The conditional divisor datum cut by a base-changed presentation section.
   271	
   272	The explicit `hsec` hypothesis is the non-vacuous fibrewise nonvanishing input.  It is
   273	converted componentwise to the injectivity required by the fibrewise-regular section
   274	construction; the integral fibre instance is installed from the standing geometrically
   275	irreducible curve hypotheses.
   276	-/
   277	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   278	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   279	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   280	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   281	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   282	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   283	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   284	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   285	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   286	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   287	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   288	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   289	  D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s
   290	    (fun j q => by
   291	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   292	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   293	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)
   294	
   295	/-- The conditional section construction preserves the base-changed datum's Picard class. -/
   296	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange_picClass
   297	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   298	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   299	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   300	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   301	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   302	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   303	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   304	    (P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange B y hsec).picClass =
   305	      (P.datum.baseChange B).cechPicClass := by
   306	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   307	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   308	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   309	  unfold sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   310	  exact D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass s
   311	    (fun j q => by
   312	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   313	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   314	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)
   315	
   316	/-- The presentation identifies datum `H^0` with native global sections of its line bundle. -/
   317	noncomputable def moduleSectionsEquiv (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   318	    Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[P.cover.Carrier] Γ(P.module, ⊤) :=
   319	  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv P.module_iso.symm 0).trans
   320	    (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   321	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   322	      isTerminalTop
   323	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   324	        (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module))
   325	
   326	/-- The native section is exactly the datum section transported through `module_iso`. -/
   327	theorem module_iso_inv_datumSection (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   328	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   329	    (P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op (⊤ : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens))).hom
   330	      (P.datumSection y) = P.moduleSectionsEquiv y := by
   331	  exact Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀_naturality
   332	    (hT := isTerminalTop) (f := P.module_iso.inv) y
   333	
   334	/-- A datum `H^0` class, read as a global section of the native pushforward. -/
   335	noncomputable def pushforwardSectionOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   336	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   337	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   338	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module, ⊤) := by
   339	  change Γ(P.module,
   340	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   341	      (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))
   342	  simpa using P.moduleSectionsEquiv y
   343	
   344	/-- The canonical unit-lift of a datum `H^0` class to the source of evaluation. -/
   345	noncomputable def evaluationLiftOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   346	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   347	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
   348	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   349	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   350	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module),
   351	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   352	        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens)) :=
   353	  ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   354	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).unit.app
   355	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   356	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).app
   357	          (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens) (P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y)
   358	
   359	/-- Evaluation of the canonical unit-lift returns the original native global section.
   360	
   361	This is the right triangle identity of pullback-pushforward.  It is the counit compatibility

+/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/
+
+/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.
+
+The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
+the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
+than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
+def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
+    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
+  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
+      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
+      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
+        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}
+
+/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
+theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
+    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
+    (U : (relCurve C L).Opens)
+    (hU : (U : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
+    (rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L ∩ U).Nonempty := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hmem⟩ := Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints C L U hU
+  exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨p, hp, rfl⟩, hmem⟩⟩
+
+/-- Every point in the dense image has residue degree one, by its retained section certificate. -/
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage'
+    {k : Type u} [Field k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
+    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
+      (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
+  intro x hx
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
+  rw [← hpx]
+  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp
+

+section DropPackage
+
+variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
+  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
+  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
+
+/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.
+
+`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
+divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
+`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
+returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
+the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
+kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
+structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
+  m : ℕ
+  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
+  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
+    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
+  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
+  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
+    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
+      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
+  genusValue : ℕ
+  excess : ℕ
+  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
+  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
+  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
+    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
+  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
+  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
+    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
+  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
+  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
+  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
+    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
+      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
+        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
+      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
+        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
+          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
+            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
+
+/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
+base-field translating divisor.
+
+The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
+with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
+`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
+`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
+structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
+    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
+  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
+  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
+  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
+  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
+  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
+    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
+  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
+    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
+  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
+    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
+  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
+    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
+  translated : IsSplitWitness C
+    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))
+
+/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
+rank-one witness.
+
+The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
+`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
+`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
+line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
+the conclusion. -/
+theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
+    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
+    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
+    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
+  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
+    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
+      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
+      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
+      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
+  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
+  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
+      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
+        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
+    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
+    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
+    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
+      hW₀, hSZ]
+    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
+    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
+    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
+      pow_zero, one_mul]
+  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
+      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
+    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
+      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
+  exact ⟨{
+    S := S
+    Z := Z
+    nonnegative := hS0
+    degree := hSdeg
+    support := hSsupport
+    baseClass := hSZ
+    h0_one := hS0one
+    h1_vanishing := hS1
+    translated := htranslated
+  }⟩
+
+end DropPackage
+

+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneTranslatedCover
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.SepPointsDense
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TangentIdentitySection
+import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ClosedPoint
+
+/-!
+# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover
+
+The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
+chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
+rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
+is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
+open TopologicalSpace Opposite
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
+
+/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
+    {K : Type u} [Field K]
+    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
+    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
+    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
+    {x : X.left}
+    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
+    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
+  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
+  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
+  have hmap :
+      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
+        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
+    ext c
+    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
+      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
+      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
+      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
+    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
+    rfl
+  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
+    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
+  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
+  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
+  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
+  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
+  rw [← hmap]
+  exact h
+
+/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
+    {k : Type u} [Field k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
+    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
+    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
+      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
+  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
+    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
+    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
+  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
+  · rfl
+
+/-! ## Image-set packaging -/
+
+theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
+    {k : Type u} [Field k]
+    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
+    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
+      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
+      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
+    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
+  intro x hx
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
+  rw [← hpx]
+  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
    12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
    13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
    14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
    15	index per point of `T`".
    16	
    17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
    18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
    19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
    20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
    21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
    22	connection is what this file supplies.
    23	
    24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    25	
    26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
    27	
    28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
    29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
    30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
    31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
    32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
    33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
    34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
    35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
    36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
    37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
    38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
    39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
    44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
    45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
    47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
    48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
    50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
    51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
    53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
    54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
    55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
    56	-/
    57	
    58	set_option autoImplicit false
    59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    60	
    61	universe u
    62	
    63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    64	
    65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    66	
    67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    70	
    71	noncomputable section
    72	
    73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
    74	
    75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
    76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
    77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
    78	
    79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
    80	
    81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
    82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
    83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
    84	
    85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
    86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
    87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
    88	
    89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
    90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
    91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
    92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
    96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
    98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
    99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
   100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
   101	
   102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
   152	
   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
   186	
   187	end
   188	
   189	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6
    11	
    12	A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.
    13	
    14	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
    15	`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
    16	**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
    17	that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
    18	open residues.
    19	
    20	**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**
    21	
    22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
    23	
    24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
    25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
    26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
    27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
    28	*membership of the locus* needs.
    29	
    30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
    31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
    32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
    33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
    34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,

     9	/-!
    10	# COV-1 input 1: the twisted class splits with a COMPUTABLE Čech representative
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean` says every plus class over a field is `relPicMk` of an honest
    13	Čech class over *some* finite separable extension.  For the coverage theorem (`w4-datb` §1.2)
    14	that is not enough by itself: the class under test is the *twisted* class
    15	`λ_t · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and COV-1 must know what its presenting Čech class IS, because step 2
    16	of the route computes the presenting class's DEGREE and steps 4–5 build a witness divisor
    17	inside that class.  A bare `∃ M` gives the degree of nothing.
    18	
    19	## What this file adds
    20	
    21	`exists_splitting_chartTwist` splits the twisted class **and identifies the presenting
    22	class** as
    23	
    24	  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`,
    25	
    26	where `M₀` presents the untwisted fibre class over the same `L`.  So the twist survives
    27	the splitting *as an explicit factor*, and its degree is computable by the landed ledger:
    28	`classDeg` of a base-changed class is base-field invariant (E-iv-alg,
    29	`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`), so the twist contributes exactly
    30	`m·d₁ − deg Z` and nothing else.
    31	
    32	Two landed facts make this cheap, and both were established by this lane earlier today:
    33	
    34	* `chartTwist_collapse` (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) — the twist is ONE
    35	  `thetaFamily`, at the single base class `chartTwistClass C m Z`.  There is no product of
    36	  families to split.
    37	* `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv` (`Picard/ThetaShift.lean:122`) — a θ-family is
    38	  **already honest at every affine test**: its affine collapse is the plus *unit* of the
    39	  base-changed base class, with no cover and no extension.  So the twist factor needs no
    40	  splitting at all; only the `λ`-factor does.
    41	
    42	That second point is the content.  A reader who expects "split a product of two plus
    43	classes" would look for a common refinement of two étale covers.  There is none to find:
    44	one factor is honest over every base, so the splitting of the product is the splitting of
    45	the other factor.
    46	
    47	## Main declarations
    48	
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk` — a θ-family is honest at
    50	  every affine test: its collapse is the plus *unit* of the base-changed base class.
    51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_base_comp` — the base comparison factors through any
    52	  intermediate field of the tower.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit` — **the twisted class
    54	  splits with its presenting class NAMED**: `M₀ · (twist class base-changed to L)`.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` — the positional introduction rule
    56	  for `IsSplitWitness`, and the retraction below.
    57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self` — its `L := K` case.
    58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass` — what COV-1 consumes: a witness
    59	  divisor for the named class certifies `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class.
    60	
    61	## A RETRACTION this file carries
    62	
    63	`isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` is a positional introduction rule for `IsSplitWitness`,
    64	which this lane had recorded as **impossible** (the closing note of
    65	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`, and memory item I-0564: "measured three times, do not retry").
    66	The old measurement tested five ways of handing the twelve components to *one* anonymous
    67	constructor, and all five do time out.  It did not test **staging** them: eight `Exists.intro`s
    68	in sequence cost nothing at the default heartbeat budget, because `L` is fixed at the first
    69	step and the two curve spellings never race as metavariables.  The trivial splitting `L := K`,
    70	named in that record as the variant worth wanting, follows in one line.  See the theorem's
    71	docstring for the diagnosis and the corrected rule.
    72	-/

    92	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    93	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

    99	/-! ## The θ-family is honest at every field point -/
   100	
   101	variable (C) in
   102	/-- **A θ-family is honest at every affine test**, in the `PicEtAff` spelling the split
   103	predicate uses: its affine collapse is the plus unit of `relPicMk` of the base-changed base
   104	class.
   105	
   106	This is `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv` (`Picard/ThetaShift.lean:122`) plus
   107	`relPicAlgMap_mk`, and it is the reason the twist needs no splitting: `PicEtAff.unit` is
   108	already the honest reading, so no étale cover ever enters for this factor. -/
   109	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk
   110	    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
   111	    picEtAffineEquiv C A (thetaFamily C L₀ (overSpec k A))
   112	      = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A)
   113	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k A) L₀)) := by
   114	  rw [thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv C L₀ A, relPicAlgMap_mk]
   115	  rfl
   116	
   117	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   118	variable (C) in
   119	/-- **The base-change comparison composes**: the relative-curve comparison down to the base
   120	factors through any intermediate field of the tower.  Both sides are `C ◁ Spec` of a
   121	`k`-algebra map into `L`, and there is only one such map out of `k`. -/
   122	theorem relCurveMap_base_comp {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   123	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L] :
   124	    relCurveMap C k L
   125	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K L)).left ≫ relCurveMap C k K := by
   126	  rw [relCurveMap, relCurveMap, ← Over.comp_left, ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
   127	  refine congrArg (fun ψ : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k k => (C ◁ ψ).left)
   128	    (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)
   129	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))
   130	    = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))
   131	      ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))
   132	  rw [← Spec.map_comp]
   133	  refine congrArg Spec.map (CommRingCat.hom_ext ?_)
   134	  exact (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k K L).symm ▸ rfl

   136	/-! ## The twisted class splits, with its presenting class named -/
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **COV-1 input 1: the twisted class splits, and its presenting Čech class is named.**
   140	
   141	If the untwisted plus class `μ` over the field `K` is presented over the finite separable
   142	extension `L/K` by the Čech class `M₀`, then the *twisted* class
   143	`μ · thetaFamily (chartTwistClass m Z)` is presented over the SAME `L` by
   144	
   145	  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`.
   146	
   147	No second extension, no common refinement of covers: the twist factor is honest over every
   148	base (`picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk`), so it passes through the splitting
   149	of `μ` untouched, as a multiplicative factor of the presenting class.
   150	
   151	This is what makes the degree of the presenting class computable, which is what `w4-datb`
   152	§1.2 steps 2–4 spend: `classDeg L` of the second factor is `classDeg k (chartTwistClass)`
   153	by E-iv-alg, hence `m·d₁ − deg Z`.  A bare `∃ M` splitting would leave that unavailable. -/
   154	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit
   155	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   156	    [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
   157	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   158	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
   159	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
   160	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
   161	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K
   162	        (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K)))
   163	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
   164	          (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))) := by
   165	  -- the twist factor's fibre at `L`: honest over `K`, then transported to `L`
   166	  have hθ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K
   167	        (thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K)))
   168	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
   169	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))) := by
   170	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk C (chartTwistClass C m Z) K,
   171	      show PicEtAff.map C L
   172	            (PicEtAff.unit C K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K)
   173	              (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k K) (chartTwistClass C m Z))))
   174	          = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K L)
   175	              (relPicMk C (overSpec k K)
   176	                (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k K) (chartTwistClass C m Z))))
   177	        from PicEtAff.map_unit C L _]
   178	    refine congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C L) ?_
   179	    rw [relPicAlgMap_mk]
   180	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)) ?_
   181	    -- `relCurveMap C k K ∘ (base change K → L)` and `relCurveMap C k L` are the same
   182	    -- whisker, since both are `C ◁ Spec` of the unique `k`-algebra map to `L`.
   183	    rw [relCurveMap_base_comp C (K := K) (L := L), Scheme.CechPic.map_comp]
   184	    rfl
   185	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, hM₀, hθ, ← map_mul, ← map_mul]

   187	/-! ## The introduction rule COV-1 uses
   188	
   189	Read the docstring of `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` before editing anything here: it
   190	retracts a standing negative result of this lane, and the retraction is what makes the
   191	corollaries possible. -/
   192	
   193	variable (C) in
   194	/-- **THE `IsSplitWitness` INTRODUCTION RULE — the one this lane recorded as impossible.**
   195	
   196	A presenting Čech class over a finite separable `L`, plus a witness divisor inside it, gives
   197	`IsSplitWitness`.  Nothing here mentions `θ`, `Σ` or a twist; the twisted case is the
   198	corollary below.
   199	
   200	**This RETRACTS the "no positional introduction rule exists" record** of
   201	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note and of the memory item filed with it.  That
   202	record was measured, and its measurement was right about what it tested — five variants, all
   203	timing out at 1000000+ heartbeats:
   204

   206	* the witness clause pre-bundled as a `have`;
   207	* either curve spelling normalised to the other;
   208	* `(isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness …).mpr` applied to the twelve-tuple;

   222	co-signed definition; the actual fix is a tactic-level one.  Measured, not inferred: this
   223	theorem's own body is the evidence, and the twisted corollary below consumes it. -/
   224	theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness
   225	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   226	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
   227	    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
   228	    (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   229	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
   230	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M))

   235	  refine Exists.intro L ?_
   236	  refine Exists.intro ‹Field L› ?_
   237	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra k L› ?_
   238	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra K L› ?_
   239	  refine Exists.intro ‹IsScalarTower k K L› ?_
   240	  refine Exists.intro ‹Module.Finite K L› ?_
   241	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra.IsSeparable K L› ?_
   242	  refine Exists.intro M ?_
   243	  exact ⟨hM, W, hW, hW1⟩

   249	At a field where the class is *already* honest, no extension is needed: a witness divisor over

   260	theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self

   286	theorem isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass

    10	/-!
    11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
    14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
    15	
    16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
    17	
    18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
    19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
    20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
    21	anywhere in the statement.
    22	
    23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
    24	
    25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
    26	
    27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
    28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
    29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
    30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
    31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
    32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
    33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
    34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
    35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
    36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
    37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
    38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
    39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
    40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
    41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
    42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
    43	
    44	## What this buys, stated exactly
    45	
    46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
    47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
    48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
    49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
    50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
    51	this tree.
    52	
    53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
    54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
    55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
    56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
    57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
    58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
    59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
    60	
    61	## What this does NOT do
    62	
    63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
    64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
    65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
    66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
    67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
    68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
    69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
    70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
    71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
    72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
    73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
    74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
    75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
    76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
    77	
    78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
    79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
    80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
    81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
    82	
    83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
    84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
    85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
    86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
    87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
    88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
    89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
    90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
    91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
    92	
    93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
    94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
    95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
    96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
    97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
    98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
    99	
   100	## Main declarations
   101	
   102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
   103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
   104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
   105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
   106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
   107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
   108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
   110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
   111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
   112	  arbitrary field.
   113	-/

   131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
   132	
   133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
   134	
   135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
   136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
   137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
   138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map

   140	
   141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
   142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
   143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
   147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
   148	  rfl

   150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
   151	
   152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
   153	
   154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
   155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
   156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
   157	
   158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
   159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
   160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
   161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
   164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
   165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
   166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
   167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
   168	
   169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
   170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
   171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
   172	
   173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
   174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
   175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
   179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
   181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
   182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
   183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
   184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩

   186	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

   188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
   189	
   190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
   191	class, at genus `0`.
   192	
   193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
   194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
   195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
   196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;

   200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
   201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
   202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
   203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   220	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   222	  refine D.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero hg p ?_
   223	  rw [D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
   224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
   225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _

   227	/-! ## The engine, with no fibrewise hypothesis -/
   228	
   229	/-- **The rigid engine from a `pic⁰` membership**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite
   230	projective over `B`, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   231	
   232	No fibrewise clause appears in the statement: the hypotheses are the membership, its
   233	presentation, and the engine's own `IsNoetherianRing B`. -/
   234	theorem rigidEngine_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
   235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :
   239	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
   240	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
   241	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   242	  D.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h)
   243	
   244	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE, FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP** — the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1` at every
   245	prime of the test ring, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   246	
   247	This is the cohomological output the classical seesaw argument consumes next.  What it does not
   248	supply is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`; see the module docstring. -/
   249	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   250	    [IsNoetherianRing B] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   251	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   252	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   253	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   254	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   255	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   256	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h) p
   257	
   258	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

   260	/-! ## The presentation binder is FREE for classes from `relPic`
   261	
   262	The correction recorded in the module docstring, made usable.  `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
   263	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) holds at an arbitrary test **ring**, so for a `pic⁰` class whose
   264	underlying `picEt` class comes from `relPicToPicEt` the presentation is not a hypothesis at
   265	all — it is produced, and with it the datum. -/
   266	
   267	/-- **The presentation, produced at a test ring**, for a class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.
   268	
   269	No field, no curve section, no `IsProper`-flavoured input beyond the standing binders: the
   270	ring-level affine-consistency lemma gives the `unit` form directly, and
   271	`exists_datum_pic0_presentation` upgrades it to the datum form. -/
   272	theorem presentation_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   273	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   274	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
   275	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   276	      picEtAffineEquiv C B (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z)
   277	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) :=
   278	  exists_datum_pic0_presentation C B π _ ⟨z, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C B z⟩
   279	
   280	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE WITH NO PRESENTATION BINDER**, for a degree-zero class coming from a
   281	relative Picard class over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring, at genus `0`.
   282	
   283	This is the form the earlier statements should have had: the only hypotheses left are the
   284	membership itself, that the class comes from `relPic` (`hz`), the covering datum and the
   285	engine's `IsNoetherianRing`.  The datum is existentially produced rather than supplied.
   286	
   287	**Non-vacuity of `hz`, stated at the level it is actually known.**  `hz` holds at the trivial
   288	class (`map_one`, verified), so the statement is not empty.  Whether it holds at a *non-trivial*
   289	degree-zero class is precisely the open surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` discussed above — the
   290	classes satisfying it form the intersection of `pic0Subgroup` with a subgroup, and this file
   291	does not measure that intersection.  So: non-vacuous, and non-vacuous at a degenerate value
   292	until that surjectivity lands. -/
   293	theorem exists_rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   294	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   295	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   296	    (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   297	    (hg : genus C = 0) (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   298	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B))
   299	    (hz : (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B)) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z) :
   300	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   301	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   302	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := presentation_of_relPicToPicEt C B π z
   303	  exact ⟨D, fun p => D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ hg lam (by rw [hz]; exact hD) p⟩
   304

   313	theorem P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (k : Type u) [Field k]
   314	    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   315	    {π : (P1.asOver k).left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   316	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum (P1.asOver k) B π)
   317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = (P1.asOver k).hom)
   318	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
